summary: Ambiguous rate shift after timezone boundary causing split billing lines
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightCall AI reports that their finalized invoice contains two adjacent line items for the same microbatch job where one line is billed at the negotiated dedicated rate and the other at the hosted/standard rate. Impact: Unexpected extra charge (approx $1,200) on March invoice for a single-day run; customer is flagged to finance and paused autopay pending clarification. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east-1; reserved capacity active; billing pipeline daily postbacks processed to billing-queue. Steps to reproduce / observed behavior: 1) Customer ran a scheduled microbatch at 2026-03-01T23:50:00-05:00 (US/Eastern). 2) Postbacks show two distinct postback timestamps: 2026-03-02T04:50:12Z and 2026-03-02T05:01:08Z. 3) First postback assigned tenant pricing tag BLOOM-DYN-2026 and the second got HOSTED_STD. 4) Billing aggregator created two lines which ended up on the finalized invoice. Logs/attachments: billing postback payloads, invoice PDF, sample postback IDs: pbk_86f9a4 and pbk_86f9bd attached to ticket. Customer expectation: single blended/negotiated reserved rate for entire microbatch run. Request: explain cause and issue credit for the hosted-rate line if our system misattributed it.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support pulled postback traces from postback-service and raw messages from SQS. Observed that both postbacks originate from the same serving node but different worker threads. Timeline: 2026-03-02 04:50:12Z (postback pbk_86f9a4) - pricing tag BLOOM-DYN-2026 applied via reserved-rate-lookup service. 2026-03-02 05:01:08Z (postback pbk_86f9bd) - pricing tag fallback to HOSTED_STD. Hypotheses: 1) Clock normalization bug: tenant metadata lookup used local wallclock (America/New_York) for one thread and UTC for the other during the DST boundary maintenance window; 2) Pricing cache eviction: reserved-rate cache entry expired between microbatches and was not refreshed for second postback; 3) Duplicate postback from retry path caused different routing through the pricing-engine which applied default tag. Queries run: - billing.postbacks.find({postback_id: { $in: ["pbk_86f9a4","pbk_86f9bd"] }}) - reserved_rates.get_for_tenant(tenant_id=brightcall-prod) => returned BLOOM-DYN-2026 for window 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z - 2026-03-31T23:59:59Z. Observed pricing-engine logs show a 504 to rate-lookup-cache at 2026-03-02T05:00:59Z. Correlation: 05:00:59Z cache 504 coincides with second postback being processed at 05:01:08Z. Postback ordering: evidence of reordering in SQS – delayed visibility on one message. Additional note: March 1–2 is near a scheduled maintenance that included a rolling cache flush on the pricing-engine.
comments: 2026-03-08 14:12 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Acknowledged ticket to customer, requested invoice + postback IDs; asked for a go-ahead to pull postback payloads from the account. Customer confirmed and provided pbk_86f9a4 and pbk_86f9bd.

2026-03-09 09:03 - Tomás Green (Billing Eng): Pulled traces and saw pricing-engine 504 around 05:00:59Z; flagged potential race between cache eviction and postback processing. Tentatively assigning P2 and will repro in staging.

2026-03-09 10:45 - Elena Ruiz (SRE): Found SQS visibility timeout tuning in us-east rolling deploy logs; one postback experienced delayed requeue. Suggested replay postback through billing-aggregator to see outcome after cache warmup.

2026-03-09 16:20 - Tomás Green (Billing Eng): Replayed pbk_86f9bd in staging after warming rate cache; it now resolves to BLOOM-DYN-2026. Confirms transient pricing cache failure was root cause for tag mismatch.

2026-03-10 08:55 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Notified customer we are preparing a credit and will reprocess the two postbacks to issue corrected invoice. Asked customer if they want immediate credit or adjustment on next invoice. Customer requested immediate credit to clear autopay hold.
resolution: Root cause: transient rate-lookup cache failure during a rolling cache flush combined with SQS delayed visibility caused one postback to be processed while the pricing-engine returned a 504 and defaulted to HOSTED_STD. Fix applied: 1) Hotfix to billing-aggregator added defensive retry + backoff for pricing-engine 5xx responses and a short-lived local cache fallback to avoid applying default host rate. 2) Reprocessed affected postbacks with warmed cache and created an adjustment credit for $1,214.30 applied to BrightCall AI account on 2026-03-10. 3) Updated runbook to avoid rolling cache flushes during high-volume scheduled microbatches for dedicated tenants. Follow-ups: monitoring alert added for pricing-engine 5xx spike and an audit job to detect adjacent-line differing-rate items within same job; engineering task INT-719 to review cache eviction policy (linked).
follow_up_actions: ENG: INT-719 - review and adjust pricing-engine cache TTL and eviction windows
SRE: add pricing-engine-5xx alert with paging (oncall)
OPS: update runbook to block rolling cache flushes for dedicated tenants during scheduled microbatches
BILLING: add reconciler check for adjacent lines with same job_id but different rate_tag
